slides.reasoning: Design A delivers the brief's near-black/lime system with condensed hero numerals, a dramatic labeled ARR curve and disciplined margins, while Design B leaves large dead zones, uses generic type, and introduces off-palette red/cyan marker rings.

Design A honors clay-dominant editorial warmth with a genuine hand-drawn journey, taped callout and buddy tag, whereas Design B defaults to a flat three-node timeline on blush (wrong dominant), with centered orphan lists and a large empty mid-band.

Design A's crisp azure/vermilion rules, tangled-to-graph before/after and single dominant $780k read instantly, while Design B's chevron blob, unlabeled circles and leader lines colliding with the 'One Identity Graph' text look structurally unresolved.

Design A's orbital allocation ring, restrained serif and gold/coral accents match the institutional brief precisely, while Design B's plain donut adds off-palette sage and white wedges with an under-used lower-left area.

Design A keeps brushed silver dominant with an exploded technical render, precise callouts and keynote-scale wordmark; Design B substitutes generic dark stock photography with a pasted-on label and a graphite panel that abandons the specified silver dominance.

Design A builds one coherent monospaced chart system with variance markers and a clearly emphasized activation gap, while Design B's single descending line conflates regions with activation and its 'ACTIVATION' and 'TARGET 75%' labels physically collide.

Design A constructs a true transit-map strategy diagram with interchange and north-star spur in the exact civic palette; Design B reduces the pillars to four bars, adds an off-palette ochre line and floats an awkward black 'North Star' disc in loose space.

Design A's chevron swimlanes, diamond gates, week ruler and ownership annotations form a dynamic roadmap; Design B falls back on four large rectangles with dashed gate lines and a generic footer bar, the very card grid the brief warns against.

Design A's bold 4C loop, marker-style annotations and mapped worked example are genuinely instructional, while Design B crams captions inside circles until text nearly touches the edges and leaves a large blank lower third under an orphaned 'Practice rule' label.

Design A's 100-square waffle, expressive 68%/54% typography and diagrammed three-app journey with confidence-break annotation are far richer than Design B's plain donut and three labeled circles, which also lose the respondent attribution and implication emphasis.

Design A achieves the auditorium keynote moment with oversized dissolving type, cyan visible/hidden UI diagram and silhouetted crowd; Design B uses a literal stock audience photo, a banner-style title bar and boxed lists that read as a template slide.

Design A's orange/powder-blue split with oversized editorial numerals, customer quote and numbered priorities is one confident composition, while Design B's serif headline, inconsistent number scales and half-empty blue box leave the layout slack and hierarchy flat.

Design A makes a detailed corridor map the emotional centerpiece with a field-ledger card, scale bar and legend; Design B's mismatched tropical stock photo with scattered orange bars reads as arbitrary overlay and its email/footnote sit in low-contrast dead zones.

Design A's enormous annotated 'a' with yellow counter, baseline/x-height rules and three same-baseline comparison specimens is properly instructional; Design B's leader lines stop short of the letterform, pointing at empty space, and the letter is too small to teach from.

Design A pairs a striking citrus macro collage with a sharply structured audience bar, dotted moment leaders and one clear investment figure, while Design B relies on generic buffet stock photography, a legend-only audience bar, and a contact line nearly lost against the image edge.
